CHIEF COMPLAINT: Right flank pain.

HPI: 48-year-old man with no significant past medical history who presents with 8 hours of severe right flank pain radiating to the groin, rated 10/10, colicky, associated with nausea and vomiting. He reports dysuria but no fever, no hematuria noted. Similar episode 2 years ago that passed spontaneously.

PMH: Nephrolithiasis (2024).

MEDS: None.

SH: Works as a truck driver. Drinks 1-2 sodas daily, minimal water. No tobacco.

ROS: Flank pain, nausea, vomiting, dysuria as above. Denies fever, chills.

EXAM:
VS: T 98.9 F, HR 102, BP 148/92, RR 18, SpO2 98% RA.
Abd: Soft, right CVA tenderness marked.
GU: No testicular tenderness.

LABS/IMAGING:
Labs: WBC 10.8, Creatinine 1.2, UA: large blood, 20-30 RBCs.
CT abdomen/pelvis without contrast: 6 mm proximal right ureteral stone with moderate hydronephrosis.

ASSESSMENT: 48-year-old man with acute right ureteral nephrolithiasis with hydronephrosis.

PLAN:
1. Ureteral stone with hydronephrosis
- Urology consult; tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily for medical expulsive therapy
- Pain control, antiemetics, IV fluids
2. Nausea/vomiting
- Ondansetron PRN
3. Stone prevention counseling
- Increase water intake, limit sodium; 24-hour urine metabolic workup as outpatient
